reason: Bash calls in this episode were refused repeatedly (cd-compound-read, assigned-variable, too-complex, multi-cd, no-rule-match), so the syntax check, chmod and the local test never ran. A global rule on call shape lets future sessions avoid the same dead ends.

In the mealie episode, three Bash calls were refused for shape alone: a `curl | python3 -c` pipeline (multi-operation), a `$(...)` token that could not be checked, and a `docker compose ... && echo OK` chain. A `grep -r` was blocked by the guard hook. The same class of refusal recurred, so the skill should name the working alternatives.

This episode had three Bash refusals the skill doesn't name: an inline env prefix before `docker compose`, a standalone `python3 -c` with no pipe, and a `curl -o ...; grep` chain. The first two are new shapes.
Two more refusal shapes seen this episode: a raw docker compose call with --env-file and a '||' fallback chain, neither covered by the existing bullets.

The loaded skill already warned against recursive grep, but the agent still tried Bash grep, a `;` chain, and `git -C` forms, each refused. Naming the `git -C` and chained forms and pointing to the Grep/Glob tools makes the rule actionable for the search step.

The agent chained bash -n, --help, --bogus, shellcheck and echo rc=$? in one call and it was refused; it loaded this skill only after three refusals. The trigger should fire before composing compound calls, not after.
Single-command script checks were refused even in the simplest shape, and the agent needed a clear rule that an unrun check is not a passed check.

Within one session a for-loop using a shell variable was refused as uncheckable, and the same search as a single grep over an explicit glob list (with --exclude='*.env') was accepted. The skill lists variable-assignment refusals but not loop-variable refusals.
The Grep tool was absent in this session, and the guard blocked a recursive grep over docs/ until --exclude='*.env' was added. The skill assumes the Grep tool always exists, so it needs the fallback.

Skill was consulted after refusals; it covers python3 -c but not `python3 -m unittest`, which was refused in the same shape even as a single absolute-path command. Recording the observed refusal so the next session plans for it.

Episode showed the agent trying three install variants (a `which || (apt || pip)` chain, pip, apt, pip --target) after the first was refused; all required approval. The skill covers chaining and refusals generally but not the install case, so the next session would repeat the same retries.
